health.emptyBody: Add your website and we will check 25 technical SEO basics for you.

https.title: Secure connection (HTTPS)
https.pass: Your site uses a secure HTTPS connection.
https.issue: Your site does not use HTTPS. Browsers mark it as “Not secure” and Google prefers secure sites.
https.fix: Turn on a free SSL certificate in your hosting panel (often called Let's Encrypt), then send all pages to the https:// address.

http_to_https.title: Redirect to the secure address
http_to_https.pass: Visitors who type http:// are sent to the secure https:// address.
http_to_https.issue: The http:// version of your site does not redirect to https://, so Google may see two copies of your site.
http_to_https.fix: Add a permanent (301) redirect from http:// to https:// in your hosting panel or website settings.

title.title: Page titles
title.issue: Some pages have no title. The title is the blue headline people click in Google.
title.fix: Give every page a unique title that says what the page is about.

title_length.title: Title length
title_length.pass: Your titles have a good length.
title_length.issue: Some titles are shorter than 30 or longer than 65 characters. Google may cut long titles, and short ones waste space.
title_length.fix: Write titles of about 30 to 65 characters with the main topic near the start.

meta_description.title: Page descriptions
meta_description.pass: Your pages have descriptions for Google.
meta_description.issue: Some pages have no description. Google then shows random text from the page under your title.
meta_description.fix: Add a short description (meta description) to each page. Most website builders and SEO plugins have a field for it.

meta_description_length.title: Description length
meta_description_length.pass: Your descriptions have a good length.
meta_description_length.issue: Some descriptions are shorter than 70 or longer than 160 characters.
meta_description_length.fix: Aim for 70 to 160 characters that describe the page and invite the click.

h1.title: Main heading (H1)
h1.pass: Each page has one main heading.
h1.issue: Some pages have no main heading or more than one. The main heading tells Google what the page is about.
h1.fix: Use exactly one H1 heading per page, usually the visible page title.

heading_structure.title: Subheadings
heading_structure.pass: Longer pages are split into sections with subheadings.
heading_structure.issue: Some long pages have no subheadings (H2). Long blocks of text are hard to read for people and for Google.
heading_structure.fix: Split long pages into sections with clear H2 subheadings.

canonical.title: Main page address (canonical)
canonical.pass: Your pages tell Google which address is the main one.
canonical.issue: Some pages do not say which address is the main version, or they point to another website.
canonical.fix: Add a canonical link to each page that points to its own main address. SEO plugins usually do this for you.

robots_txt.title: Instructions for search engines (robots.txt)
robots_txt.pass: Your robots.txt file lets Google read your site.
robots_txt.issue: Your robots.txt file is missing or blocks your whole site from Google.
robots_txt.fix: Make sure yoursite.com/robots.txt exists and does not contain “Disallow: /” for all search engines.

sitemap.title: Sitemap
sitemap.pass: We found a sitemap that lists your pages.
sitemap.issue: We could not find a sitemap. It helps Google find all of your pages.
sitemap.fix: Create a sitemap (most website builders and SEO plugins can do this), then add it to robots.txt and Google Search Console.

noindex.title: Hidden from Google (noindex)
noindex.pass: None of the checked pages is hidden from Google.
noindex.issue: Some pages tell Google not to show them in search results.
noindex.fix: Remove the “noindex” setting from pages that should appear in Google. Check the visibility settings of your website.

viewport.title: Mobile friendly
viewport.pass: Your site is set up for mobile screens.
viewport.issue: Your site is not set up for mobile screens. Most visitors use a phone, and Google looks at the mobile version first.
viewport.fix: Add the mobile viewport tag (width=device-width) or switch to a responsive theme.

html_lang.title: Page language
html_lang.pass: Your pages say which language they are written in.
html_lang.issue: Your home page does not say which language it is written in.
html_lang.fix: Set the lang attribute on the html tag, for example lang="en". Theme settings often have this option.

hreflang.title: Language versions (hreflang)
hreflang.pass: Your language versions are linked correctly.
hreflang.issue: Your site has pages in several languages, but they are not linked to each other correctly.
hreflang.fix: Add hreflang links so Google shows each visitor the right language version.

open_graph.title: Social media preview
open_graph.pass: Links to your site show a title and an image on social media.
open_graph.issue: When someone shares your site, social networks may show no image or the wrong title.
open_graph.fix: Add Open Graph tags (og:title and og:image). SEO plugins usually have a “Social” section for this.

structured_data.title: Structured information for Google
structured_data.pass: Your home page gives Google structured information about your business.
structured_data.issue: Your home page has no structured information, or it contains errors. It helps Google show extras such as ratings and opening hours.
structured_data.fix: Add structured data (Schema.org, for example Organization or LocalBusiness). Many SEO plugins can do this.

image_alt.title: Image descriptions
image_alt.issue: Some images have no description (alt text). Google and screen readers cannot tell what they show.
image_alt.fix: Add a short description to each meaningful image in your media library.

broken_links.title: Broken links
broken_links.issue: Some links on your site lead to pages that do not exist.
broken_links.fix: Update or remove these links, or redirect the old addresses to a working page.

duplicate_titles.title: Same titles
duplicate_titles.pass: Every page has its own title.
duplicate_titles.issue: Some pages share the same title, so Google cannot tell them apart.
duplicate_titles.fix: Give each page a unique title.

duplicate_descriptions.title: Same descriptions
duplicate_descriptions.pass: Every page has its own description.
duplicate_descriptions.issue: Some pages share the same description.
duplicate_descriptions.fix: Write a unique description for each page.

thin_content.title: Short pages
thin_content.issue: Some pages have fewer than 300 words. Very short pages rarely rank well in Google.
thin_content.fix: Add useful information to these pages, or combine similar short pages.

ttfb.title: Server speed
ttfb.pass: Your server starts answering quickly ({{value}} ms).
ttfb.issue: Your server needs {{value}} ms to start answering. Slow pages lose visitors and rankings.
ttfb.fix: Turn on caching, use a CDN, or ask your hosting company for faster hosting.

page_size.title: Page size
page_size.pass: Your home page is light and loads quickly.
page_size.issue: The code of your home page is large, which makes it slow on phones.
page_size.fix: Remove unused plugins and code, and avoid putting large content directly into the page.

favicon.title: Site icon (favicon)
favicon.issue: Your site has no icon. Google shows it next to your result on phones.
favicon.fix: Upload a square site icon in your website or theme settings.

thin_content.title: Content is very short ({{value}} words)
thin_content.fix: Go deeper: add sections that answer the questions readers would ask. Google rarely ranks short posts highly.

short_content.title: Content is short ({{value}} words)
short_content.fix: Bring it above 600 words with examples, steps or frequently asked questions.

no_meta_description.title: No meta description
no_meta_description.fix: In your SEO plugin (Yoast, Rank Math), write an inviting 70–160 character description for the post.

meta_description_length.title: Meta description length is off ({{value}} characters)
meta_description_length.fix: Keep it between 70 and 160 characters; longer ones get cut off in Google.

title_length.title: Title length is off ({{value}} characters)
title_length.fix: Keep the title between 30 and 65 characters, with the main keyword near the start.

no_subheadings.title: No subheadings
no_subheadings.fix: Split the post into sections with H2 subheadings; it helps both readers and Google.

no_internal_links.title: No links to other pages on your site
no_internal_links.fix: Add 2–3 links to related products, categories or other posts.

missing_alt.title: {{value}} images have no description (alt text)
missing_alt.fix: In the media library, add a short description of what each image shows.

no_images.title: No images
no_images.fix: Add at least one image that illustrates the topic; posts with images are read longer.

outdated.title: Not updated for {{value}} days
outdated.fix: Review facts, prices and dates and update the post; Google prefers fresh content.
